image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a classic car wheel featuring a chrome wire-spoke rim and a whitewall tire. The wheel is mounted on a light green vehicle fender. The rim has a prominent central bullet-nose hubcap and intricate wire spokes radiating outward. The tire shows a distinct white sidewall band and black tread area.

artifact_observations.location: Wire spokes near the central hub
artifact_observations.reasoning: Some of the inner wire spokes appear slightly fused or lack distinct separation where they meet the central hub assembly, likely due to AI generation smoothing or resolution limits, though it mimics real-world depth-of-field blur.
The line separating the whitewall from the black tire wavers slightly in thickness, which can occur in AI generations, though it is subtle and could be attributed to tire deformation.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific sub-type (wire wheel vs. alloy) and ensure the image aligns with the 'car wheel' taxonomy despite the complex geometry.
Wire wheels are prone to AI artifacts like melting or broken connections. This expert will verify if each spoke is a distinct, continuous topological entity connected to both the rim and the hub.
To ensure the central spinner/hubcap sits correctly in front of the spokes and that the spokes have consistent depth relative to the rim, checking for spatial collapse.
Chrome reflections are difficult for AI to render accurately. This expert will check if the reflections on the hubcap and rim are physically consistent with the environment.

focus_areas: Continuity and distinctness of individual wire spokes
Physical plausibility of the central hubcap connection
Consistency of chrome reflections across curved surfaces
Boundary sharpness between whitewall and black tire
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the topology of the wire spokes. In AI-generated wire wheels, spokes often merge into each other or fail to connect cleanly to the hub. Verify if the 'fusion' noted in artifacts is actual structural failure or just optical blur. Check if the reflections on the chrome hubcap match a coherent light source direction.
